title: Esther Chapter 10 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Esther chapter 10 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Esther Chapter 10 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Esther Chapter 10.

questions.question: In Esther 10, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The king Ahasuerus laid a tribute upon the land
Mordecai the Jew was next unto king Ahasuerus
Mardocheus said, God hath done these things
questions.correctAnswer: The king Ahasuerus laid a tribute upon the land
questions.explanation: This is found in Esther 10:1, which states that the king laid a tribute upon the land.

questions.question: Who laid a tribute upon the land and the isles of the sea?
questions.explanation: Esther 10:1 clearly states that the king Ahasuerus laid a tribute.

questions.question: What is written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia?
questions.explanation: Esther 10:2 mentions the declaration of the greatness of Mordecai as being recorded in the chronicles.

questions.question: Who was great among the Jews and accepted by the multitude of his brethren?
questions.explanation: Esther 10:3 specifies that Mordecai was great among the Jews and accepted by his brethren.

questions.question: What did Mordecai seek for his people?
questions.explanation: Esther 10:3 states that Mordecai was seeking the wealth of his people.

questions.question: What did Mordecai speak to all his seed?
questions.explanation: Esther 10:3 mentions that Mordecai spoke peace to all his seed.

questions.question: What did Mardocheus say?
questions.explanation: Esther 10:4 records that Mardocheus said, 'God hath done these things.'

questions.question: What does Mardocheus remember?
questions.explanation: Esther 10:5 states that Mardocheus remembers a dream which he saw concerning these matters.

questions.question: Did anything of the dream Mardocheus saw fail?
questions.explanation: Esther 10:5 indicates that nothing thereof hath failed.

questions.question: Was Mordecai next unto king Ahasuerus?
questions.explanation: Esther 10:3 confirms that Mordecai was next unto king Ahasuerus.

questions.question: Is the greatness of Mordecai acknowledged in the text?
questions.explanation: Esther 10:2 states the declaration of the greatness of Mordecai.

questions.question: True or False: The king Ahasuerus is mentioned in Esther 10.
questions.explanation: Esther 10:1 mentions the king Ahasuerus.

questions.question: True or False: Mordecai was accepted by the multitude of his brethren.
questions.explanation: Esther 10:3 states that Mordecai was accepted by the multitude of his brethren.

questions.question: True or False: Mardocheus said he had a vision.
questions.explanation: The text says Mardocheus remembered a dream, not a vision, as per Esther 10:5.

questions.question: True or False: Mordecai sought the destruction of his people.
questions.explanation: Esther 10:3 states that Mordecai sought the wealth and peace of his people, not their destruction.

medium.title: Esther Chapter 10 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Esther Chapter 10 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What does the river represent in Esther 10:6?
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because Esther 10:6 states, 'this river is Esther, whom the king married, and made queen.'

questions.question: What does Esther 10:7 indicate about the two dragons?
options: They represent the king and queen
They represent the Jews and Gentiles
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'the two dragons are I and Aman,' indicating Mordecai and Haman.

questions.question: What did Esther 10:8 mention about the nations?
options: They were allies of the Jews
They were assembled to destroy the name of the Jews
questions.correctAnswer: They were assembled to destroy the name of the Jews
questions.explanation: This is confirmed in Esther 10:8, which says, 'the nations were those that were assembled to destroy the name of the Jews.'

questions.question: According to Esther 10:9, who cried to God and were saved?
questions.explanation: Esther 10:9 states, 'my nation is this Israel, which cried to God, and were saved.'

questions.question: What does Esther 10:10 signify about the lots?
options: One was for the Jews, another for the Gentiles
questions.correctAnswer: One was for the Jews, another for the Gentiles
questions.explanation: Esther 10:10 clearly states, 'Therefore hath he made two lots, one for the people of God, and another for all the Gentiles.'

questions.question: What promise is associated with the acts of Ahasuerus in Esther 10:1?
questions.explanation: Esther 10:2 indicates that the acts of Ahasuerus and Mordecai are recorded, thus they will be remembered.

questions.question: How is Mordecai described in Esther 10:3?
questions.explanation: Esther 10:3 states, 'For Mordecai the Jew was next unto king Ahasuerus.'

questions.question: What does Esther 10:4 affirm about God's actions?
options: God will act in the future
questions.explanation: This affirmation is found in Esther 10:4, which states, 'Then Mardocheus said, God hath done these things.'

questions.question: According to Esther 10:5, what did Mordecai remember?
questions.explanation: Esther 10:5 indicates that Mordecai remembered a dream, stating, 'For I remember a dream which I saw concerning these matters.'

questions.question: What is the relationship between Esther 10:6 and Esther 10:7?
questions.explanation: Esther 10:6 describes Esther and identifies her as a river, while Esther 10:7 expands on the characters involved, linking Mordecai and Haman.

questions.question: What lesson can be drawn from Esther 10:9 about prayer?
options: God hears the prayers of His people
No one needs to cry out to God
questions.correctAnswer: God hears the prayers of His people
questions.explanation: Esther 10:9 highlights that Israel cried to God and were saved, showing that God responds to the prayers of His people.

questions.question: What does Esther 10:10 imply about God's justice?
questions.explanation: The verse indicates that God made lots for both His people and the Gentiles, implying impartiality in His justice.

questions.question: Does Esther 10:1 mention a tribute laid by King Ahasuerus?
questions.explanation: Esther 10:1 states, 'And the king Ahasuerus laid a tribute upon the land, and upon the isles of the sea,' confirming the statement is true.

questions.question: Is it true that Mordecai was disliked by the Jews according to Esther 10:3?
questions.explanation: Esther 10:3 states that Mordecai was 'accepted of the multitude of his brethren,' indicating he was not disliked.

questions.question: Is it true that Esther 10:8 says the nations were there to help the Jews?
questions.explanation: Esther 10:8 indicates that the nations were assembled to destroy the name of the Jews, not to help them.

hard.title: Esther Chapter 10 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Esther Chapter 10.

questions.question: According to Esther 10:11, when did the two lots come before God among all nations?
options: At the hour, and time, and day of judgment
At the beginning of the year
At the time of the king's decree
questions.correctAnswer: At the hour, and time, and day of judgment
questions.explanation: Esther 10:11 states that the two lots came at the hour, time, and day of judgment before God among all nations.

questions.question: What did God do for His people according to Esther 10:12?
options: Remembered his people and justified his inheritance
Sent a prophet to warn them
questions.correctAnswer: Remembered his people and justified his inheritance
questions.explanation: Esther 10:12 clearly states that God remembered his people and justified his inheritance.

questions.question: In Esther 10:13, which month and days are established for assembly, joy, and gladness before God?
options: The month Adar, the fourteenth and fifteenth day
The month Nisan, the tenth and eleventh day
The month Tishrei, the first and second day
The month Elul, the twentieth and twenty-first day
questions.correctAnswer: The month Adar, the fourteenth and fifteenth day
questions.explanation: Esther 10:13 specifies that the days are in the month Adar, on the fourteenth and fifteenth day, for assembly and joy before God.

questions.question: What is the nature of the celebration described in Esther 10:13?
options: An assembly, joy, and gladness before God
A military parade and victory feast
questions.correctAnswer: An assembly, joy, and gladness before God
questions.explanation: Esther 10:13 describes the days as a time of assembly, joy, and gladness before God among the generations.

questions.question: According to Esther 10:11, what is the significance of the timing of the two lots?
options: They came at the day of judgment before God
They coincided with the king’s birthday
They were cast during a solar eclipse
They arrived at the time of the new moon
questions.correctAnswer: They came at the day of judgment before God
questions.explanation: Esther 10:11 emphasizes that the two lots came at the hour, time, and day of judgment before God among all nations, highlighting divine timing.

questions.question: What does Esther 10:12 imply about God's relationship with His people?
options: God is faithful and justifies His inheritance
God is wrathful and punishes his people
questions.correctAnswer: God is faithful and justifies His inheritance
questions.explanation: Esther 10:12 shows that God remembered His people and justified His inheritance, indicating faithfulness and justice.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'Adar' in Esther 10:13 refer to?
options: The twelfth month of the Hebrew calendar
A type of ancient Persian coin
The name of the king’s palace
questions.correctAnswer: The twelfth month of the Hebrew calendar
questions.explanation: In Esther 10:13, 'Adar' refers to the twelfth month of the Hebrew calendar, during which the festival of Purim is celebrated.

questions.question: Which literary device is primarily used in Esther 10:11 with the phrase 'hour, and time, and day'?
questions.explanation: Esther 10:11 uses parallelism by repeating similar temporal terms 'hour, and time, and day' to emphasize the precise moment of judgment.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of God remembering His people as in Esther 10:12?
questions.explanation: Psalm 105:8 says, 'He remembers his covenant forever,' which echoes the theme of God remembering His people in Esther 10:12.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage fulfills the theme of divine judgment in Esther 10:11?
questions.explanation: Revelation 20:12 describes the final judgment before God, fulfilling the theme of the day of judgment mentioned in Esther 10:11.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes Esther 10:11 in the chapter?
options: The establishment of two lots, one for God’s people and one for the Gentiles
The decree of the king to impose tribute
The dream of Mordecai about Esther and Aman
The celebration of the feast of Purim
questions.correctAnswer: The establishment of two lots, one for God’s people and one for the Gentiles
questions.explanation: Esther 10:10 states that two lots were made, one for God's people and one for the Gentiles, which immediately precedes the timing described in Esther 10:11.

questions.question: What is the typology represented by 'a little fountain became a river' in Esther 10:6?
options: Esther as a source of blessing expanding to many
The growth of the Persian empire
The rise of the Babylonian captivity
questions.correctAnswer: Esther as a source of blessing expanding to many
questions.explanation: Esther 10:6 uses this imagery typologically to represent Esther’s influence growing from a small source to a large blessing for many.

questions.question: How does the phrase 'with gladness before God, according to the generations for ever among his people' in Esther 10:13 illustrate the concept of inclusio?
options: It brackets the chapter by emphasizing perpetual celebration
It signals the end of the festival
questions.correctAnswer: It brackets the chapter by emphasizing perpetual celebration
questions.explanation: Esther 10:13 closes the chapter with a phrase that echoes earlier themes of God's enduring covenant, creating an inclusio that brackets the narrative with perpetual joy.

questions.question: True or False: Esther 10:12 indicates that God abandoned His people after their deliverance.
questions.explanation: Esther 10:12 states that God remembered His people and justified His inheritance, indicating His continued care rather than abandonment.

questions.question: True or False: Esther 10:13 establishes a permanent annual festival for the Jewish people in the month of Adar.
questions.explanation: Esther 10:13 declares that the days in the month of Adar shall be observed with assembly and joy forever among the people, establishing a permanent festival.

theological.title: Esther Chapter 10 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Esther Chapter 10 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Esther 10:4 teach about God's providential role in human affairs?
options: God sovereignly directs history according to His will
God passively observes human decisions without intervention
God primarily acts through natural disasters to discipline nations
God's role is limited to spiritual matters, not political outcomes
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly directs history according to His will
questions.explanation: Esther 10:4 states, 'God hath done these things,' indicating a doctrine of God's providence and sovereign direction in the unfolding events.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning divine assurance and fulfillment is taught in Esther 10:5?
options: God ensures the fulfillment of His promises without fail
Human dreams are the ultimate source of divine revelation
God's promises are conditional on human strength
Prophecies may fail and require reinterpretation
questions.correctAnswer: God ensures the fulfillment of His promises without fail
questions.explanation: Esther 10:5 says, 'nothing thereof hath failed,' underscoring God's faithfulness in fulfilling His plans and promises.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine election and the identity of God's people is conveyed by Esther 10:9?
options: God has chosen Israel as His covenant people and delivered them
Salvation is universal without distinction between peoples
God's promises apply exclusively to Gentile nations
Israel's deliverance is purely political without divine involvement
questions.correctAnswer: God has chosen Israel as His covenant people and delivered them
questions.explanation: Esther 10:9 emphasizes 'my nation is this Israel, which cried to God, and were saved,' affirming election and salvation of Israel.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Esther 10:12 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Esther 10:12 states, 'So God remembered his people, and justified his inheritance,' illustrating God's faithfulness to His covenant promises.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is prominently displayed in Esther 10:1 regarding the king's imposition of tribute?
questions.explanation: The king's authority to lay tribute, as noted in Esther 10:1, reflects God's sovereign rule over earthly powers.

questions.question: How does Esther 10:3 theologically connect to the theme of intercession found elsewhere in Scripture?
options: Mordecai's role as a mediator seeking peace for his people parallels Christ's intercession
Mordecai's political ambition contradicts biblical intercession
The chapter rejects intercession as unnecessary for salvation
Intercession is only for Gentiles, not God's chosen people
questions.correctAnswer: Mordecai's role as a mediator seeking peace for his people parallels Christ's intercession
questions.explanation: Esther 10:3 describes Mordecai 'seeking the wealth of his people, and speaking peace,' paralleling the mediatorial role of Christ interceding for His people (cf. Romans 8:34).

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection is illustrated by the imagery in Esther 10:6?
options: Esther as a river symbolizes the life-giving salvation flowing from the Messianic queen
Esther represents worldly power without spiritual significance
The river imagery denotes judgment upon Israel
The reference to the sun and water denies God's involvement in history
questions.correctAnswer: Esther as a river symbolizes the life-giving salvation flowing from the Messianic queen
questions.explanation: In Esther 10:6, the 'little fountain became a river... this river is Esther,' symbolizing abundant salvation and blessing, typologically connected to Messianic blessings.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Esther 10:10 and 10:11 teach about divine judgment and election?
options: God has appointed distinct destinies for His people and the Gentiles, revealed at the appointed time
Judgment is arbitrary and unrelated to election
The two lots represent human free will without divine involvement
Salvation is universal and not divided between peoples
questions.correctAnswer: God has appointed distinct destinies for His people and the Gentiles, revealed at the appointed time
questions.explanation: Verses 10 and 11 speak of 'two lots,' one for God's people and one for Gentiles, coming 'at the hour, and time, and day of judgment,' teaching sovereign election and eschatological judgment.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine deliverance and eschatological hope is taught in Esther 10:12 and 10:13?
options: God remembers and justifies His people, establishing perpetual joy and assembly
Deliverance is temporary and not commemorated
Eschatological hope is unrelated to Israel's historic experiences
God's people are left without assurance of future restoration
questions.correctAnswer: God remembers and justifies His people, establishing perpetual joy and assembly
questions.explanation: Esther 10:12-13 affirms that God 'remembered his people' and established days of assembly and joy forever, teaching ongoing divine deliverance and eschatological hope.

questions.question: What combined theological insight do Esther 10:7 and 10:8 offer about spiritual conflict and God's people?
options: There is a cosmic struggle involving God's people and their enemies
The conflict is purely political without spiritual dimension
God's people are always victorious without opposition
Spiritual conflict is irrelevant to Israel's identity
questions.correctAnswer: There is a cosmic struggle involving God's people and their enemies
questions.explanation: Verses 7 and 8 describe 'the two dragons' (Mordecai and Aman) and the nations assembled to destroy the Jews, illustrating spiritual warfare themes.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Esther 10:1-3 teaches that political power is independent of divine sovereignty. What does the text actually teach?
options: God's sovereignty undergirds political authority and the elevation of Mordecai
Political power is random and unrelated to divine will
Mordecai's rise is purely human ambition without divine involvement
The king acts without any divine influence or purpose
questions.correctAnswer: God's sovereignty undergirds political authority and the elevation of Mordecai
questions.explanation: Esther 10:2-3 affirm God’s providential role in Mordecai’s advancement, showing that political authority operates under divine sovereignty.

questions.question: What doctrine does Esther 10:13 teach about the continuity of divine worship and covenant remembrance?
options: God's covenant people celebrate deliverance perpetually with joy and assembly
Worship and remembrance are temporary and obsolete
Covenant celebrations are purely cultural without theological basis
Divine worship is replaced by secular festivities
questions.correctAnswer: God's covenant people celebrate deliverance perpetually with joy and assembly
questions.explanation: Verse 13 states that the days in Adar are celebrated 'according to the generations for ever,' showing the perpetuity of covenant remembrance and worship.

questions.question: Which divine attribute best explains the establishment of the two lots in Esther 10:10?
questions.explanation: The division of the two lots for God's people and Gentiles in Esther 10:10 reflects God's attribute of justice in dealing rightly with different peoples.

questions.question: What theological synthesis is drawn from Esther 10:2 and 10:3 regarding leadership among God's people?
options: God raises leaders who are accepted by both the king and their people for the welfare of the nation
Leaders are chosen solely by political power without regard to community acceptance
Divine empowerment excludes human approval in leadership
Leadership is a human construct unrelated to divine sanction
questions.correctAnswer: God raises leaders who are accepted by both the king and their people for the welfare of the nation
questions.explanation: Verses 2 and 3 describe Mordecai as next to the king and accepted by his brethren, showing divine raising of leaders with dual approval.

questions.question: How does Esther 10:9 reflect the doctrine of salvation history as unique to Israel in contrast to Gentile nations?
options: God wrought signs and wonders not done among the Gentiles, showing Israel's unique covenant relationship
Israel's salvation is identical to Gentile experiences without distinction
Signs and wonders are common among all nations equally
God saves all nations in the same manner without election
questions.correctAnswer: God wrought signs and wonders not done among the Gentiles, showing Israel's unique covenant relationship
questions.explanation: Verse 9 states God worked wonders not done among Gentiles, emphasizing Israel's distinct covenantal salvation history.
